summary: An executor that finished its work files one immutable submission whose report binding reads pending, and the daemon seals a bundle for it only once the terminal report is accepted and all six seal checks hold. Each unsealing case names one durable fact the checks read, so a check wired to the wrong record changes the answer here rather than passing quietly.

unsealing.summary: Nothing has been accepted about the work, so the three checks that read the binding all fail and the submission stands unsealed.
The accepted report describes a tree the submission does not propose, so the acceptance is evidence about something else.
The Run reported that its work is not ready, and sealing it would make the report's own conclusion unreadable downstream.
The claim names a path the lease never made writable, so the work reaches outside the scope the Run was dispatched under.
The workspace was rematerialized after the claim, so the tree being proposed came from a generation the lease no longer points at.
The lease names a different base commit than the claim started from, so what the work would be applied to is not what it was written against.
